advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a case where the post-merge conflict lands on a path the tickets branch does NOT track, asserting _resolve_conflicted_apply logs and removes it (foreign branch), not restore-from-HEAD.
evidence: foreign = [p for p in unmerged if path_is_foreign_to_branch(base, p)]
In the test, only shared.txt conflicts; shared.txt is committed on the tickets branch (seed), so path_is_foreign_to_branch returns False and the foreign bucket stays empty
assert not (tracker / "src" / "leak.py").exists() passes because git stash apply <sha> never touches the foreign stash entry — not because _resolve_conflicted_apply's foreign branch executed
advisory.finding: The new foreign-path branch of _resolve_conflicted_apply (classify unmerged paths as foreign, logger.warning, and remove untracked paths via discard_unmerged_paths) is not exercised through push.py: the new interfaces test only produces a conflict on shared.txt, which is a TRACKED/regenerable path, so the foreign bucket is always empty on this path. The leak.py/raced.py absence assertions pass because the by-sha apply never applies the foreign stash at all, not because the foreign-removal code ran.
scenarios: A regression that mis-classifies a foreign conflicted path as regenerable (restoring from HEAD instead of removing) would not be caught by this test — only by the separate stage_and_commit test in test_store_write_unmerged_recovery.py
